## Threading

`threading.Thread` for background work; join before printing final lines for stable stdout.

exercises.title: Goroutine
exercises.description: Launch Python sayHello(). Print main done. Use time.Sleep to let Pythonroutine run.
exercises.solution:
import threading
import time

def say_hello():
    time.sleep(0.05)
    print("Hello!")

print("main done")
t = threading.Thread(target=say_hello)
t.start()
t.join()

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: Create ch := make(chan string). Send "ping" to ch in Pythonroutine, receive and print.
exercises.solution:
import queue
ch = queue.Queue()

def sender():
    ch.put("ping")

import threading
threading.Thread(target=sender).start()
print(ch.get())

exercises.title: Buffered Channel
exercises.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 2. Send 10 and 20 without blocking. Then receive and print both.
exercises.solution:
import queue
ch = queue.Queue(maxsize=2)
ch.put(10)
ch.put(20)
print(ch.get(), ch.get())

exercises.title: Select Statement
exercises.description: Create two channels ch1 and ch2. Send to ch1 in Pythonroutine after 10ms. Use select to receive whichever comes first.
exercises.solution:
import queue, threading, time

ch1 = queue.Queue()
ch2 = queue.Queue()

def send():
    time.sleep(0.01)
    ch1.put("from ch1")

threading.Thread(target=send).start()
print(ch1.get())

exercises.title: Fan-In Pattern
exercises.description: Create two Pythonroutines that each send a string to a shared channel. Use a third Pythonroutine to fan-in (read) from the channel and print received values. Close the channel when both senders are done.
hints: Use wg.Add(2) for the two sender goroutines
In a third goroutine, defer close(ch) after wg.Wait()
Range over ch to collect all values
exercises.solution:
import queue, threading

ch = queue.Queue(maxsize=2)

def send(msg):
    ch.put(msg)

threading.Thread(target=send, args=("hello",)).start()
threading.Thread(target=send, args=("world",)).start()
print(ch.get())
print(ch.get())

exercises.title: WaitGroup
exercises.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch 3 Pythonroutines that each print their number, then wait for all to complete before printing "done".
exercises.solution:
import threading

def work(n):
    print(n)

for i in range(1, 4):
    t = threading.Thread(target=work, args=(i,))
    t.start()
    t.join()
print("done")
